answer: Because the ember lockup is upheld by the lotus escrow, the kernel audit can verify the release date and an early withdrawal attempt is rejected. The bond is locked for 16 epochs and cannot be withdrawn or transferred, so capital committed to an alias is unavailable for the whole term. Running a large swarm thus freezes capital at scale for the full period, which is a cost that honest participants pay once per identity. That is 9 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
